A parity matrix can have a zero time block even when it has full row rank, so a nonzero injection can remain invisible after random modulation. stage_tex.matched: The analysis is organized around three results. First, using the fixed-window kernel identity as preliminary algebra, we characterize all deterministic zero-prehistory attacks that preserve every overlapping residual, obtain an overlap-rank existence condition, and connect their causal realization to finite-time estimation displacement. Autonomous attacks on fully attacked windows are then analyzed separately under explicit spectral assumptions. Second, a structural nondegeneracy test supports the fixed-attack KL result and an explicit finite-window energy bound for independent random injections under an existing watermark. Third, a residual-energy decision rule is calibrated under the nominal Gaussian model and connected to fixed-attack asymptotic detection power. The energy bound concerns the encoded injection; its interpretation does not extend automatically to decoded disturbance, switched-estimator stability or estimation-error recovery. The analytical examples illustrate these distinctions without claiming comparative simulation superiority.

stage_tex.matched: This paper studies false data injection on measurement-sharing links in distributed state estimation with finite-window parity residuals. A deterministic injection preserves the residual distribution exactly when its stacked vector belongs to the kernel of the parity matrix. With a healthy prehistory and continuous sliding-window monitoring, all deterministic residual-preserving attacks admit a causal realization driven by the null space of the overlap observation matrix. This gives an exact finite-onset existence condition and a separate test for nonzero receiver displacement; a three-state example exhibits damage with no start-up or termination residual. Autonomous attacks on fully attacked windows are analyzed separately under explicit spectral conditions. Using an existing independently refreshed multiplicative watermark, we identify a nondegeneracy condition under which a fixed stealthy injection produces divergent residual Kullback--Leibler (KL) divergence. The argument uses a Gaussian maximum-entropy bound and does not assume that the attacked residual is Gaussian. For finite-second-moment attacks jointly independent of the watermark sequence and nominal noise, a fixed KL budget yields an explicit bound on the total encoded injection energy, proportional to the inverse square of the watermark variance. A nominally calibrated residual-energy detector separates the implementable decision rule from the distribution-level budget; a fixed-attack asymptotic power result connects the watermark analysis to that detector. Analytical examples distinguish degenerate windows, temporal watermark refreshing and packet-dependent attacks. The guarantees concern specified windows and attack information and do not assert vanishing decoded disturbance or universal estimation-error recovery.

First, using the fixed-window kernel identity as preliminary algebra, we characterize all deterministic zero-prehistory attacks that preserve every overlapping residual, obtain an overlap-rank existence condition, and connect their causal realization to finite-time estimation displacement. Third, a residual-energy decision rule is calibrated under the nominal Gaussian model and connected to fixed-attack asymptotic detection power. stage_tex.matched: This paper studies false data injection on measurement-sharing links in distributed state estimation with finite-window parity residuals. A deterministic injection preserves the residual distribution exactly when its stacked vector belongs to the kernel of the parity matrix. With a healthy prehistory and continuous sliding-window monitoring, all deterministic residual-preserving attacks admit a causal realization driven by the null space of the overlap observation matrix. This gives an exact finite-onset existence condition and a separate test for nonzero receiver displacement; a three-state example exhibits damage with no start-up or termination residual. Autonomous attacks on fully attacked windows are analyzed separately under explicit spectral conditions. Using an existing independently refreshed multiplicative watermark, we identify a nondegeneracy condition under which a fixed stealthy injection produces divergent residual Kullback--Leibler (KL) divergence. The argument uses a Gaussian maximum-entropy bound and does not assume that the attacked residual is Gaussian. For finite-second-moment attacks jointly independent of the watermark sequence and nominal noise, a fixed KL budget yields an explicit bound on the total encoded injection energy, proportional to the inverse square of the watermark variance. A nominally calibrated residual-energy detector separates the implementable decision rule from the distribution-level budget; a fixed-attack asymptotic power result connects the watermark analysis to that detector. Analytical examples distinguish degenerate windows, temporal watermark refreshing and packet-dependent attacks. The guarantees concern specified windows and attack information and do not assert vanishing decoded disturbance or universal estimation-error recovery.

stage_tex.matched: Finite-window parity residuals remove both the nominal state contribution and deterministic injections in the corresponding observable-trajectory subspace. Consistency across windows and an intact healthy history impose additional conditions: exact finite-onset attacks have a causal realization whose input dimension is the nullity of the overlap observation matrix. Full overlap rank excludes that class, whereas rank deficiency permits nonzero attacks; a separate reachable-output condition determines their effect on the receiver. The resulting fixed-gain bias depends on the excited modes and their coupling to the receiver. Under an existing independently refreshed multiplicative encoder, nonzero temporal-block exposure is needed for a fixed attack to produce divergent residual KL; full row rank of the parity matrix alone is insufficient. For independent finite-second-moment injections, a blockwise condition yields an explicit total encoded-energy bound at finite watermark variance. A nominally calibrated energy statistic provides an implementable decision rule, with a separate asymptotic power statement for fixed deterministic attacks. The analysis does not extend that statement to watermark-dependent attack families or infer vanishing estimation damage from encoded-energy suppression. The analytical examples identify these limits and the conditions under which the finite-window results apply.
